claim: Manual compaction and fresh contexts are presented as ways to keep the working context small while preserving useful findings in files.
The hosts use focused subagents to research separate parts of a problem before assembling the main implementation context.
Research is written and reviewed before it becomes input to an implementation plan.
The live example shows that incorrect research can survive into later work unless a human catches it.
Consistent names across a codebase reduce ambiguity for both people and coding agents.
The speakers recommend multiple human checkpoints before code review, especially around research and planning.
